_comment: D5 regression case list. The runner reads this file only; pass/fail is decided from the structured RESULT_FILE each simulation writes, never from log text.

cases.name: neg_wrong_golden
cases.note: negative control: the checker must reject a deliberately wrong golden
cases.causality: inject: the expected value of every beat is XORed with 1, so no beat can match. check: the comparator must fire on every beat, i.e. ITS_DATA_MISMATCH and data_errors both equal the beat count. forbidden: every other id, and any effect on done_errors.

cases.name: neg_illegal_desc
cases.note: negative control: width 2 must raise the sticky protocol error
cases.causality: inject: a descriptor with width 2, which the wrapper rejects. check: the DUT raises its sticky protocol_error, which the monitor edge-detects exactly once, so ITS_PROTOCOL_ERROR is exactly 1. forbidden: any beat, any data or done mismatch, any other id.

cases.name: rand
cases.note: constrained random draw of legal cases, fixed seed so a failure can be replayed

cases.name: neg_lfnst_xform
cases.note: LFNST enabled with a non-zero transform type, illegal per wrapper:775
cases.causality: inject: an LFNST descriptor with a non-zero transform type. check: rejected at the descriptor gate, so the sticky error is asserted and edge-detected once -> ITS_PROTOCOL_ERROR exactly 1, and no TU ever runs. forbidden: any beat, any other id.

cases.name: neg_lfnst_mode3
cases.note: LFNST mode 3 is not an allowed encoding, see wrapper:780
cases.causality: inject: LFNST mode 3, which is not an allowed encoding. check: rejected at the descriptor gate -> ITS_PROTOCOL_ERROR exactly 1, no TU runs. forbidden: any beat, any other id.

cases.name: neg_addr_overrun
cases.note: beat addressed past the TU's last point, caught at wrapper:2434
cases.causality: inject: one beat addressed past the TU's last point. check: the DUT accepts the descriptor and still retires the TU, but flags the overrun once (ITS_PROTOCOL_ERROR exactly 1) and the beat that hit the wrong region cannot match the golden. The mismatch count is bounded rather than fixed: at least one beat must differ, and no more beats can differ than were produced. forbidden: any other id, any done mismatch.

cases.name: neg_stray_end
cases.note: end marker with no TU outstanding, caught at wrapper:2438
cases.causality: inject: an end marker while no TU owns the slot. check: the DUT flags it once (ITS_PROTOCOL_ERROR exactly 1) and must not manufacture output. forbidden: any beat, any data or done mismatch, any other id.

cases.name: neg_no_end
cases.note: fill never closed, so the TU must never produce a beat
cases.causality: inject: a TU whose end marker is never sent. check: the TU never drains, so check_phase reports the one stranded TU exactly once -> ITS_INCOMPLETE_TU exactly 1, pending exactly 1, and zero beats. forbidden: any beat, any other id.

cases.name: neg_short_beats
cases.note: truncated input closes the TU but cannot reproduce the golden
cases.causality: inject: the input stream stops before the descriptor is satisfied. check: the TU still retires, but the output cannot reproduce the golden, so at least one beat must mismatch. The exact count is bounded, not fixed, because which beats cover unfilled locations depends on the write order. forbidden: any protocol error (the handshake itself stays legal), any other id.

cases.name: reset_mid_tu
cases.note: reset while beats are streaming; only the post-reset TU must complete

cases.name: vseq_multi_agent
cases.note: virtual sequence drives the stimulus agent while the back-pressure agent changes profile underneath it

cases.name: neg_zero_data
cases.note: end marker inside the pre-fill scrub window: the DUT retires the TU with no data, so it cannot reproduce the golden
cases.causality: inject: the end marker arrives inside the pre-fill scrub window, so the TU retires with no data fed. check: the TU completes (tus exactly 1) with zero fill, which cannot reproduce the golden, so at least one beat must mismatch; the count is bounded because the beat-to-region map depends on the fill order. forbidden: any protocol error, any other id.

cases.name: neg_desc_flood
cases.note: four descriptors pushed while the scrub window blocks bind_event, tripping the queue-full guard
cases.causality: inject: four descriptors pushed while the scrub window holds bind_event low, so the queue overflows. check: the DUT flags the rejected descriptor once (ITS_PROTOCOL_ERROR exactly 1), no TU ever completes, and the descriptors already queued are stranded, so check_phase reports them once and pending is at least 1 (the exact number left behind depends on how far the queue drained). forbidden: any beat, any data or done mismatch, any other id.

cases.name: neg_end_only_fill
cases.note: end-only marker after the fill window opened: no data command, so the slot completes without a phantom write
cases.causality: inject: an end marker with no data beat after the fill window opened. check: the slot closes without a phantom write, the TU retires (tus exactly 1), and with no data fed the output cannot reproduce the golden, so at least one beat must mismatch; the count is bounded because the fill order decides which beats differ. forbidden: any protocol error, any unexpected beat, any other id.

cases.name: tail_stress
cases.note: widest TU against a long output-grant blackout: stalls the H-pass consumer so the raw-response tail buffer fills

cases.name: queued_end
cases.note: second descriptor waits in the queue and its end arrives before it binds; the DUT parks the end and retires that TU with zero data, so both TUs are checked beat by beat

cases.name: queued_end_store
cases.note: head TU closes its end inside the scrub window and retires as zero-data while the scrub still blocks bind, so the queued TU's end has to be parked in end_seen_desc[] and inherited at bind time
